headline: Bond revolts, Gulf oil shock and financial repression grind the world into stagflation

events: Weak US 30-year auctions push 10-year Treasury yield above 5.8%; term premium spikes and the dollar falls despite risk-off
Japan's 30-year JGB yield breaches 4%; BoJ resumes unlimited purchases, yen slides past 175
Israel-Iran exchange escalates into tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz; Brent touches $135 for six weeks
European gas prices triple into winter; Germany and Italy reintroduce energy price caps funded by new borrowing
US raises tariffs on remaining Chinese goods; China restricts rare-earth magnet and gallium exports to the US and allies
AI capex boom stalls as financing costs rise; two hyperscalers cut data-center budgets by a quarter
Synchronised global recession: world growth ~0.6%, euro area and UK contract
French OAT-Bund spread blows out past 300bp after budget collapses; ECB activates TPI with conditionality, triggering street protests
UK gilt crisis mark two forces emergency spending cuts and a BoE bond backstop
Egypt, Pakistan, Kenya and Argentina default or restructure; IMF resources stretched thin
Record heat dome over South Asia and failed monsoon cut Indian and Pakistani grain output; India bans rice exports
US election held amid 6.5% unemployment; winner campaigns on tariffs, deportations and 'cheap money'
Fed, under new leadership, introduces de facto yield caps on 10-year Treasuries; US inflation rebounds to 6.5%
G20 average inflation peaks near 7.4% as oil, food and a weaker dollar combine
Major cyberattack takes down a G7 interbank payment system for four days, freezing wages and card payments
Serbia-Kosovo and Ethiopia-Eritrea fighting erupts; Sahel jihadist offensive reaches coastal West African states
China sustains growth via state-bank credit but youth unemployment exceeds 25%; capital controls tightened
Firms accelerate AI adoption to cut wage bills; back-office and call-centre layoffs mount across India, Philippines and Europe
Partial stabilisation: Hormuz shipping normalises under a US-Gulf-India naval convoy arrangement, Brent back near $90
Ukraine ceasefire frozen along front lines; Europe commits to 3.5% of GDP defence spend financed by joint EU bonds
Atlantic hurricane pair devastates Gulf Coast refining and Florida; US home-insurance market partly nationalised
Real interest rates negative across most advanced economies; savers and pensioners protest 'stealth default'
Solar and battery installations surge in India, Gulf states and Southeast Asia as hedge against oil volatility
Six more frontier economies seek Common Framework treatment; Sri Lanka and Ghana default for a second time
World growth limps at ~2.3%; inflation sticks near 4.5% as governments tolerate it to erode debt
Japan imposes a one-off wealth levy and extends BoJ holdings above 60% of JGBs
Trade splits into a US-aligned bloc, a China-centred bloc and a hedging 'middle' led by India, Gulf, Brazil and ASEAN
Populist parties lead governments or coalitions in France, Italy, Netherlands and Austria; EU fiscal rules suspended indefinitely
AI deployment broadens to ~30% of firms; productivity gains visible in software and finance but too small to offset debt service
Global temperature hits 1.6C on a five-year average; climate-related displacement passes 40 million people a year

winners: Gulf and other energy exporters with spare capacity
Asset-rich households holding real assets and gold
India and Vietnam as hedging 'connector' economies
Leading AI platform firms with cash-rich balance sheets
losers: Fixed-income savers and pensioners in advanced economies
Debt-distressed frontier economies in Africa and South Asia
Young renters facing high rents and stagnant real wages
Coastal homeowners in uninsurable climate-risk zones
bullets: Advanced economies run financial repression: central banks cap yields, inflation hovers 4-5%, and real rates stay negative to shrink debt ratios.
Bond markets remain the real opposition: France, UK, Italy and Japan each faced at least one acute yield spike that toppled or tamed a government.
Nine sovereign defaults or restructurings, mostly in Africa and South Asia, overwhelm a shrunken aid and IMF system.
Trade is organised into three blocs; tariffs and export controls on critical minerals, chips and food are routine policy tools.
Energy shocks from the Gulf and climate-hit refining spur a defensive renewables build-out; renewables reach ~43% of global electricity.
AI spreads to ~30% of firms, displacing ~36 million jobs cumulatively, deepening anger among clerical and service workers.
Trust in institutions sinks to the high 20s; populist governments dominate Europe and street protest over prices and pensions is chronic.
Climate disasters are an annual fiscal event, with states becoming insurers of last resort for homes, crops and infrastructure.
wildcard: A four-day cyberattack shutdown of a G7 interbank payment system in 2029 froze wages and card payments for tens of millions.
image_description: In a sweltering 2031 Marseille street, a retiree counts euro coins at a market stall where olive oil carries a ration-style price cap sticker, while an AI kiosk replaces the shuttered bank branch behind her and protest posters about pensions peel in the heat.
